result.summary: This PR unifies the 'TX decode failed' error message across eight RPCs that call DecodeHexTx(), replacing the misleading 'Make sure the tx has at least one input.' hint (originally added for #19836) with a shared constant that also mentions bad hex and truncated/padded serialization as possible causes. Array-taking RPCs (generateblock, testmempoolaccept, submitpackage) now report the failing index instead of echoing the raw hex. Tests are updated to match, and new coverage is added for malformed sendrawtransaction payloads.
result.problem: Callers hitting a transaction decode failure across different RPCs got inconsistent and sometimes misleading error text ('has at least one input' even when the real problem was bad hex or truncated data), making it harder to diagnose the actual cause.

result.card: This PR unifies the wording of 'transaction decode failed' RPC errors across eight call sites (sendrawtransaction, signrawtransactionwithkey, generateblock, testmempoolaccept, submitpackage, combinerawtransaction, importprunedfunds) using a new shared constant, replacing a misleading hint that was copied from a 2020 fix (#19836) even where the real cause was bad hex or truncated data rather than a missing input. It adds functional test coverage for malformed sendrawtransaction payloads and updates existing tests to match the new wording. The change is purely cosmetic error-text cleanup with no behavior, security, or performance impact, and is P4 in RPC, the only category it substantively belongs to (mining and wallet edits are mechanical call-site updates). The sole review comment so far, from maintainer maflcko, objects to LLM-sounding wording in the PR description and code comments rather than to the substance of the change, and the author force-pushed the same day. No dependencies or blockers are known.
